data.ruling: The refutation stands. The classic-CAN bound reads correctly. The MCP2515 data sheet gives a data frame of 44 + 8N bits in Figure 2-1, printed on page 9, not on page 8 as the claim cites. Section 2.6 on page 8 gives an interframe space of at least 3 recessive bits. That makes 47 us a frame at 1000 kbit/s, 8,511 frames in 400 ms and 64 frames in 3 ms. The claim's last sentence is false: "A CAN FD frame is longer, so the bound holds for FD traffic too". The claim itself says the tree defines no traffic on the external port, and it counts 11-bit base-format frames. On that basis an FD base-format frame (FBFF) with bit-rate switching (BRS) is shorter than 47 us at any data-phase rate of 2000 kbit/s or more. DroneCAN 4.4 names 2000, 4000, 5000 and 8000 kbit/s among its data-phase rates. So the stated maximum of 8,511 and 64 frames is not a bound for FD traffic. Scope is function, because the ruling concerns the frame count on this port, not the part. Condition that limits the ruling: if the port carries only 29-bit identifiers (DroneCAN uses extended frames), the FD extended-format frame (FEFF) is about 49 nominal bits plus 32 data-phase bits. That is 55.4 us at 5000 kbit/s and 53 us at 8000 kbit/s. Both are longer than 47 us, and the 8,511 and 64 bound would then hold. The claim does not restrict itself to 29-bit identifiers. The V20 and V21 values the verifier attributes to the P2 return (CAN FD, BRS to 5000 kbit/s) were not read. They are not in any committed return, since the results tree holds only T1. The owner's rows for V20 and V21 read "for research".
data.evidence: MCP2515 DS20001801K, re-read with pdftotext: the Figure 2-1 caption "Data Frame (number of bits = 44 + 8N)" sits on the page footed "DS20001801K-page 9". Section 2.6, Interframe Space, reads: "composed of at least three recessive bits, called the 'Intermission'". DroneCAN 4.4 "Bus rates" reads: "CANFD implementations will usually use bit rate switching (BRS) with a nominal bit rate of 1MBps, with payload switching to 1, 2, 4, 5 or 8 MBit depending on hardware capabilities". The CiA "CAN FD - the basic idea" page reads: "At the sample-point of the BRS bit, the bit rate switch is performed". It names the FDF, BRS and ESI bits and "The 3-bit stuff-bit counter is grey-coded and it is protected by a parity bit". It also states "CRC field comprises 17-bit (for frames with payloads up to 16 byte)" and says the CRC field uses fixed stuff bits. The same page elsewhere says "8-bit stuff-bit counter", which is inconsistent with the 3-bit figure; the 3-bit figure is used here. Derived here, with no dynamic stuff bits and ISO 11898-1 not read: an FBFF frame with no data is 30 bits at the nominal rate: SOF, 11-bit ID, RRS, IDE, FDF, res and BRS make 17, then CRC delimiter, ACK, ACK delimiter, 7 EOF and 3 IFS make 13. It is 32 bits at the data-phase rate: ESI 1, DLC 4, stuff count 4, CRC 17 and 6 fixed stuff bits. At 5000 kbit/s that is 30 + 6.4 = 36.4 us, 10,989 frames in 400 ms and 83 in 3 ms. At 2000 kbit/s it is 30 + 16 = 46 us, still under 47 us. The FEFF frame adds SRR, IDE and 18 identifier bits: 49 + 32/5 = 55.4 us. These counts are derived, not read from a data sheet.
